patch_description:
This version replaces the expensive general simulated annealing loop with a frontier-driven constructive search.

The main insight is that a newly created zero cell is automatically connected to the outside if it is either on the grid boundary or adjacent to an existing zero cell. Therefore, deletion candidates can be generated directly from the current zero frontier, avoiding most invalid isolated-zero proposals. The program repeatedly peels wards from the outside while preserving every required adjacency edge.

To escape local geometric dead ends, it occasionally performs adjacency-preserving nonzero-to-nonzero boundary transfers. These reshape ward boundaries without changing the score, after which frontier peeling resumes. Connectivity checking is reduced to the source ward only: the destination ward is known connected because transfers only use a neighboring destination color, and zero expansion is known connected by construction.
